### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.sessions

### Question

When I run `:lua MiniSessions.restart()` (or `:MySession restart` which you'll see below), everything works fine except it goes to INSERT mode. This wasn't happening until I updated the plugin some 8 hours ago.

This is how I set it up:

```lua
require('mini.sessions').setup {
	autoread = true,
	autowrite = true,
	file = 'Session.vim',
	verbose = { read = false, write = true, delete = true },
}

local session_subcommands = {
	save = function()
		MiniSessions.write(MiniSessions.config.file)
	end,
	load = function()
		MiniSessions.read(MiniSessions.config.file)
	end,
	delete = function()
		MiniSessions.delete(MiniSessions.config.file, { force = true })
	end,
	restart = function()
		vim.cmd 'confirm wall'
		-- SEE: https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2410
		MiniSessions.restart()
	end,
}

vim.api.nvim_create_user_command('MySession', function(args)
	local fn = session_subcommands[args.args]
	if fn then
		fn()
	else
		vim.notify('Session: unknown argument "' .. args.args .. '"', vim.log.levels.ERROR)
	end
end, {
	desc = '󱂬  session: manage sessions',
	nargs = '?',
	complete = function(subcommand)
		return vim.tbl_filter(function(sc)
			return sc:find(subcommand, 1, true) == 1
		end, vim.tbl_keys(session_subcommands))
	end,
})

```

	restart = function()
		vim.cmd 'confirm wall'
		-- SEE: https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2410

	desc = '󱂬  session: manage sessions',
	nargs = '?',
	complete = function(subcommand)

  delete = function() MiniSessions.delete(MiniSessions.config.file, { force = true }) end,
  restart = function()
    vim.cmd('confirm wall')

    MiniSessions.restart()

})

reply_data.body: Soooo. The issue was that I can a `VimEnter` autocommand that checked whether I had `Session.vim` present to detect whether I was reloading with `MiniSession.reload`, but this command *can* use a temp session file with a different name. So my autocommand was checking for `Session.nvim`, not finding it, opening telescops file picker **which puts neovim in INSERT mode**. My fix if anyone looks for this in the future (including me :smile:)

reply_data.body:
> whether I had `Session.vim` present to detect whether I was reloading with `MiniSession.reload`

If you mean `MiniSessions.restart()`, then this was never a guarantee. It [uses active or new temporary](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-sessions.html#minisessions.restart) session. If the active session comes from 'Session.vim', then it is used, but not in other cases.

reply_data.body:
@echasnovski I get it. The use case is having a way to know at VimEnter that it's starting from a session restart which is different from restoring from a `Session.vim`, or from running `nvim`, `nvim -- files or dirs`.

In my contrived use-case, I check those start up conditions on VimEnter to decided whether I should run open a file picker or not (I don't want to if nvim is restoring a session).

So I can detect a session in being restored if `Session.vim` exists, but in the case of `MiniSessions.restart` there's no way to know as it does it so cleanly.

Right now, this is what I'm doing to detect a `MiniSession.restart`:

```lua
vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>:ss', function()
	if vim.fn.filereadable(vim.fn.expand(vim.fn.getcwd() .. '/Session.vim')) == 0 then
		vim.fn.writefile({}, vim.fn.getcwd() .. '/my_restart_session')
	end
	vim.cmd 'confirm wall'
	MiniSessions.restart()
end, { desc = '󰙰  session: restart' })
```

Then, on a VimEnter autocommand I check:

```lua
if vim.fn.filereadable(vim.fn.expand(vim.fn.getcwd() .. '/my_restart_session')) == 1 then
	if vim.fn.delete(vim.fn.expand(vim.fn.getcwd() .. '/my_restart_session')) ~= 0 then
		vim.notify('error deleting my_restart_session', vim.log.levels.ERROR)
	end
	return -- this returns from the autocommand and doesn't open the file picker.
end
```

> In my contrived use-case, I check those start up conditions on VimEnter to decided whether I should run open a file picker or not (I don't want to if nvim is restoring a session).

Ah, I just now noticed that you are the same author as in #2410. There already is [a suggested solution for this case](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2410#discussioncomment-16853408). It is, of course, doable to add something like `vim.g.minisessions_restart = true` as a part of `restart lua ...` command. Maybe also together with `vim.g.minisessions_restart_pre = true` to be able to act on `VimLeave[Pre]`.

Although I'd really like to avoid having two ways of doing things in the (hopefully) near future, this might indeed be necessary. I'll think a bit more about it.
